s: Guardant Health DEF 14A filed 2026-04-28, ownership table as of 2026-04-20; GH close $170.69 on 2026-08-21 (stockanalysis.com)
m: 2,766,779 GH shares beneficially owned x $170.69 = $472M; stake is held shares, not option-heavy
did: Co-founded Guardant Health in 2013 with Helmy Eltoukhy after running technology development at the Stanford Genome Technology Center and diagnostics research at Illumina; built Guardant360 liquid biopsy, then led the Shield blood test for colorectal cancer screening approved by FDA in July 2024.
why: Digital error suppression let them call tumor DNA at very low allele fractions from a tube of blood, and they kept the CLIA lab in-house rather than licensing the assay, so they controlled turnaround, price and the reimbursement dossier end to end.
obst: Payers treated liquid biopsy as investigational and refused to pay; Guardant burned cash for six years before Medicare covered Guardant360, and had to run its own prospective ECLIPSE trial to get Shield covered.
turn: FDA approval of Guardant360 CDx in August 2020, the first liquid biopsy cleared for comprehensive tumor genomic profiling, which forced commercial payers to follow.

s: Life360 DEF 14A filed 2026-04-16, ownership as of 2026-03-31 and age table as of April 2026; LIF close $44.66 on 2026-08-21
m: 811,884 shares held directly and in three childrens trusts x $44.66 = $36M, plus 1,710,364 exercisable options at the $5.66 plan weighted-average strike = $67M intrinsic; about $104M plus prior sales
did: Co-founded Life360 in 2007 at age 23 after a Berkeley degree and Air Force service, entering a Google-sponsored contest for a family locator built for disaster response; grew it to roughly 96 million monthly users, listed it on the ASX in 2019 and on Nasdaq in 2022, and bought Tile in 2021.
why: Every install recruits the rest of the household, so customer acquisition cost is near zero and the install base compounds without paid marketing; monetization came years later by charging for crash detection, driving reports and roadside help on a base rivals would have had to buy.
obst: US growth investors passed, so the 2019 listing had to be done on the Australian exchange; COVID lockdowns collapsed location-sharing usage in 2020 and forced layoffs before the subscription mix recovered.
turn: The 2021 Tile acquisition plus the 2022 shift to a hardware-and-membership bundle, which lifted paying subscribers and justified the Nasdaq dual listing.

s: Corcept Therapeutics DEF 14A filed 2026-04-17, ownership as of 2026-04-09 and director age table; CORT close $122.25 on 2026-08-21
m: 2,398,599 shares in family trusts, a family partnership and two 2025 GRATs x $122.25 = $293M, plus 592,916 exercisable options worth roughly $55M intrinsic against a mid-30s average strike
did: Was CEO of LifeScan through its sale to Johnson and Johnson, then CEO of Neurex and COO of Syntex; became founding chairman of Corcept Therapeutics in 1999 and stayed on the board for 27 years, holding the equity through the whole Korlym and relacorilant build.
why: Corcept licensed mifepristone, an off-patent French compound nobody wanted to touch, for Cushing syndrome, an orphan indication too small for large pharma; orphan exclusivity plus a single specialty pharmacy channel gave it pricing power and no generic entrant for over a decade.
obst: Corcept had no approved product for its first 13 years and the stock traded near a dollar through 2008-2011; later it spent years in patent litigation against Teva over Korlym and absorbed a 2019 short-seller campaign over its specialty pharmacy.
turn: FDA approval of Korlym in February 2012 for Cushing syndrome, which turned a thinly capitalised licensing bet into a cash-generating specialty pharma.

s: Navan DEF 14A filed 2026-05-12, ownership as of 2026-03-31 and director age table; NAVN close $29.16 on 2026-08-21
m: 11,560,111 shares on an as-exchanged Class B basis x $29.16 = $337M, less roughly $25M of option exercise cost on the 5,951,283 option and RSU shares included
did: Co-founded TripActions with Ilan Twig in Palo Alto in February 2015 after selling StreamOnce to Jive Software; rebuilt corporate travel around a consumer-style search interface, added the Liquid card and expense product in 2020, renamed the company Navan in 2023 and listed it on Nasdaq in October 2025.
why: Incumbent travel agencies made money on per-booking fees and hid inventory behind agents; Navan gave the traveller an open search and gave finance automatic policy enforcement, then took interchange on its own corporate card, so it monetised the payment rail instead of the booking.
obst: Corporate travel went to zero in March 2020; TripActions cut a large share of staff, raised emergency debt at punitive terms, and had to build a payments business from scratch to have any revenue at all.
turn: The 2020 launch of TripActions Liquid, which converted a travel booking tool into a spend management company and carried it through the shutdown.

s: Navan DEF 14A filed 2026-05-12, ownership as of 2026-03-31 and director age table; NAVN close $29.16 on 2026-08-21
m: 12,920,326 shares on an as-exchanged Class B basis x $29.16 = $377M, less roughly $12M of exercise cost on the 2,989,136 option and RSU shares included
did: Co-founded TripActions in February 2015 as CTO after leading engineering at RockMelt and co-founding StreamOnce, sold to Jive Software in 2013; built the search and booking engine that indexes GDS, direct hotel and low-cost carrier inventory in one place, and ran engineering through the October 2025 IPO.
why: Business travel content sat in incompatible silos, so agencies competed on contracts rather than product; a single index that could return a policy-compliant fare in one search is what let the company sell control to CFOs instead of negotiating agency margin.
obst: GDS content agreements restricted what a startup could display, so the engine had to be built against direct supplier connections and NDC at a time when airlines were still refusing to open them.
turn: The 2023 rebrand to Navan, which repositioned a travel booking engine as a travel-and-expense spend platform and set up the 2025 Nasdaq listing.

s: Upstart Holdings DEF 14A filed 2026-04-16, ownership and officer age table; UPST close $30.30 on 2026-08-21; 2021 Form 4 sales reported at about $132M gross
m: 13,271,453 UPST shares held directly, in the family revocable trust, a GRAT LLC and gift trusts x $30.30 = $402M, plus roughly $90M of retained after-tax proceeds from 2021 open-market sales
did: Built and ran Google Apps as President of Google Enterprise from 2004 to 2012, taking Gmail and Docs into businesses, then founded Upstart in 2012 to underwrite consumer credit with machine learning on education and employment data rather than FICO alone; took it public in December 2020.
why: Banks priced off a score that misprices thin-file borrowers, but could not legally justify alternative variables; Upstart sold the model to banks and credit unions as white-label origination instead of lending off its own balance sheet, so it scaled without bank capital and without owning the credit risk.
obst: The stock fell from $401 in October 2021 to under $12 in 2022 when loan funding partners stepped back and Upstart had to hold loans on its own balance sheet; it cut staff twice and paused originations at some partners.
turn: The CFPB no-action letter on non-traditional underwriting variables, which made bank partnerships legally defensible and made the December 2020 IPO possible.

s: SentinelOne DEF 14A 2026, ownership as of 2026-04-30 and executive officer age table; S close $21.19 on 2026-08-21
m: 4,516,619 held shares, trust shares and near-term RSUs x $21.19 = $96M, plus 3,406,920 exercisable options worth roughly $38M intrinsic against an estimated $10 average strike
did: Co-founded SentinelOne in 2013 and built an endpoint agent that models process behaviour on the device rather than matching signatures in the cloud, with one-click rollback of ransomware damage; listed it on the NYSE in June 2021 and bought Attivo Networks in 2022 and PingSafe in 2024.
why: CrowdStrikes cloud-first design needs connectivity and analyst triage; putting detection and automatic rollback on the endpoint itself let SentinelOne win air-gapped, mid-market and MSSP-served accounts that the cloud model served poorly, and it backed that with a ransomware warranty rivals would not write.
obst: Entered a market Symantec and McAfee owned and CrowdStrike was already winning, funded years of losses to do it, and then watched the stock fall roughly 80% from its 2021 highs while absorbing two acquisitions.
turn: The June 2021 NYSE IPO followed by the 2022 Attivo Networks deal, which added identity attack surface and turned a single agent into a platform.

s: BillionToOne DEF 14A filed 2026-04-21, ownership as of 2026-03-31; age from the 424B4 prospectus of 2025-11-06; BLLN close $95.03 on 2026-08-21
m: 2,227,542 Class B shares plus 765,387 exercisable options x $95.03 = $284M, less a small option exercise cost; the 200,000 spouse shares he disclaims are excluded
did: Co-founded BillionToOne in 2016 out of a Stanford biology PhD and built quantitative counting, which tags each DNA template with a unique molecular identifier so a blood draw can count single-gene disorders; launched the UNITY prenatal screen and listed on Nasdaq in November 2025.
why: Existing prenatal screening could only detect whole-chromosome dosage, so single-gene conditions like sickle cell and cystic fibrosis needed a separate paternal sample; counting molecules rather than reading ratios opened a reimbursed category with no direct rival, billed through the companys own CLIA lab.
obst: US life-science funds passed on the single-gene claim, so early money came from Hummingbird in Europe; the company then had to build its own CLIA lab and win payer coverage indication by indication before it had meaningful revenue.
turn: The November 2025 Nasdaq IPO, which repriced a privately held diagnostics lab into a multi-billion-dollar public company and marked the founders stakes.

s: BillionToOne DEF 14A filed 2026-04-21, ownership as of 2026-03-31; age from the 424B4 prospectus of 2025-11-06; BLLN close $95.03 on 2026-08-21
m: 2,325,108 Class B shares plus 1,000 Class A and 702,693 exercisable options x $95.03 = $288M, less a small option exercise cost
did: Co-founded BillionToOne with Oguzhan Atay in 2016 after a Stanford PhD and serves as President and Chief Technology Officer, building the assay chemistry and bioinformatics behind the UNITY prenatal screen and the Northstar oncology line on the same molecular counting platform.
why: Keeping probes, chemistry, bioinformatics and the CLIA lab in-house meant every new indication reused one validated platform instead of paying a sequencing vendor per run, so gross margin improved with each product rather than being capped by a licensed instrument.
obst: The counting claim had to be validated head to head against Nateras entrenched Panorama test in payer-facing studies before any insurer would cover UNITY, which meant years of clinical spend with no reimbursement.
turn: Winning broad commercial payer coverage for UNITY, which converted a validated assay into billable volume and made the 2025 IPO possible.

s: Oruka Therapeutics DEF 14A 2026, ownership table and director age table as of 2026-04-17; ORKA close $107.96 on 2026-08-21
m: 448,720 held shares, RSUs and restricted stock x $107.96 = $48M, plus 905,300 exercisable options worth roughly $75M intrinsic against an estimated $25 average strike
did: Left a partnership at Versant Ventures to found Oruka Therapeutics in February 2024 with Fairmount and Paragon Therapeutics, in-licensing half-life-extended antibodies against IL-23 and IL-17 for plaque psoriasis, and took it public in August 2024 by reverse merger into ARCA biopharma.
why: Skyrizi and Bimzelx had already de-risked the biology, so the only unsolved variable in psoriasis was dosing frequency; in-licensing engineered antibodies aimed at twice-yearly dosing skipped discovery risk entirely and went straight at the one axis where the incumbents could be beaten.
obst: Oruka has no discovery engine of its own and depends on Paragon to generate antibodies, so it had to prove in 2025 clinical data that its half-life extension actually delivered the dosing interval, against a class where AbbVie already books billions.
turn: The August 2024 reverse merger into ARCA biopharma with a concurrent private placement, which took a four-month-old company public and funded the programs to human data.

s: Snowflake DEF 14A 2026, ownership table and executive officer age table; SNOW close $332.78 on 2026-08-21
m: 639,543 shares held directly, through two LLCs he manages and several GRATs he is trustee of, x $332.78 = $213M, plus 53,515 exercisable options
did: Ran SQL Server program management at Microsoft and then Google BigQuery before joining Snowflake in 2019 to lead product; drove Snowpark, the data sharing and marketplace model and the Cortex AI line as EVP of product through the September 2020 IPO and after.
why: Separating storage from compute let customers pay per query instead of per cluster, and making cross-account data sharing native turned the platform into a network: a companys suppliers and customers had to be on Snowflake to exchange live data, which is a switching cost a warehouse alone never had.
obst: Had to displace Teradata and Amazon Redshift inside conservative enterprise data teams, then defend a consumption revenue model in 2022 and 2023 when the same customers were told to optimise cloud spend down.
turn: The September 2020 IPO, the largest software listing to that date, which repriced the whole cloud data platform category and marked employee equity.

s: BridgeBio Pharma DEF 14A 2026, ownership as of 2026-04-01 and director age table; BBIO close $81.50 on 2026-08-21
m: 910,085 shares x $81.50 = $74M, plus 697,339 vested options worth roughly $36M intrinsic against an estimated $30 average strike
did: Led R&D at COR Therapeutics through the Integrilin approval and its sale to Millennium in 2002, then ran Portola Pharmaceuticals as CEO; co-founded BridgeBio in Palo Alto in 2015 as President of R&D and built the subsidiary structure that produced acoramidis for ATTR cardiomyopathy.
why: Each genetic-disease program sits in its own subsidiary with its own investors and its own equity, so the scientists are paid on their molecule rather than on the parent, and a failure is ring-fenced; that structure let BridgeBio run dozens of Mendelian programs on capital no single-asset biotech could raise.
obst: The lead ATTR program missed on the Part A readout of ATTRibute-CM in December 2021, cutting the stock roughly 70% and forcing a restructuring and staff cuts before the company could get to the Part B data.
turn: The July 2023 ATTRibute-CM 30-month readout showing acoramidis worked, which led to FDA approval as Attruby in November 2024 and restored the equity.
